newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Air Mauritius supports share index in mixed market.
newsitem.headline: Air Mauritius supports share index in mixed market.

text.p: A surging share price of national carrier Air Mauritius supported the Mauritius bourse index on Friday at a session in which moving stocks ended mixed, brokers said.
The Semdex edged up by 0.62 points to 364.00 in turnover of 9.15 million rupees on 417,825 shares from 48.45 million rupees on 423,804 shares on Wednesday.
The Mauritius bourse trades on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays.
Air Mauritius shares continued to climb on Friday after diving in early March because of a forecast of slumping profits for the company in the financial year ending 31 March 1997.
Air Mauritius rose by 2.30 rupees, its maximum permitted 6 percent, to 41.70 rupees on 20,197 shares.
"It looks like that the market initially over-reacted after that lower profit forecast came," one broker said.
"That forecast was much worse than anyone could have expected. This probably explains the market overreaction," he added.
Bourse officials said support of the SEMDEX on Friday was also provided by State Bank of Mauritius, another heavyweight.
State Bank of Mauritius gained 10 cents to an all-time high of 11.30 rupees on 23,200 shares.

On Thursday, State Bank officials announced that London- based Prudential Portfolio Managers had acquired a 35 percent stake in the bank's fund management subsidiary to launch an asset fund management joint venture in Mauritius.
Moving shares in the rest of the market ended mixed on Friday and traded within thin ranges, bourse officials said.
Mauritius Commercial Bank lost 50 cents to 84.50 rupees on 26,197 shares. Building materials manufacturer United Basalt Products was 70 cents down to 32 rupees on 9,000 shares.
Conglomerate Ireland Blyth was unchanged at 14.60 rupees on 199,410 shares and sugar concern Mon Tresor Mon Desert was 80 cents up to 38.80 rupees on 100 shares.
Hotel based Grand Baie Hotel was stable at 45.40 rupees on 33,464 shares and Sun Resorts was one rupee lower to 44.10 on 1,771 shares. Sun Resorts traded ex-dividend on Friday.
National Investment Trust (NIT) was 10 cents down to 10.80 rupees on 14,130 shares but Fincorp Investment rose 50 cents to 73 rupees on 1,495 shares.
